液晶テレビにつなぐと、昔のガンコン(光線銃)が撃てなくなった。なぜか知っていますか？🎯

ブラウン管(CRT)は、実は画面全体が一度に光っているわけではなく、光の点が上から下へ、1秒に約60回のペースで画面を塗り進めています。銃の先の光センサーは「光がこちらを通った瞬間」の時刻を拾い、画面のどこを狙っているかを割り出していました。灯台の光が当たった時刻から、光の向きがわかる。そんな発想に近いですね。液晶は画素が光り続けたり、内部の映像処理で表示が遅れたりするため、この「時間の手がかり」が使えなくなった、とされています。

そこで気になったのが、2025年11月13日に日本で発売された「G'AIM'E×タイムクライシス」。時間ではなく「目」で解く方式で、高解像度カメラとAIで画面を認識する、とメーカーは説明しています(センサーバー不要・HDMI接続・バンダイナムコ公式ライセンス)。プレミアムは『タイムクライシス』『ガンバレット』『スティールガンナー』1・2の4本入りで、足元のペダルを踏むと身を乗り出して撃ち、離すと隠れる、あのアーケードの操作も再現します。

では、シューティングゲームで遊ぶと注意力はどうなるのでしょう？🤔
・Green & Bavelier(Nature, 2003): アクションゲームをよく遊ぶ人は、視覚的な注意の課題で非プレイヤーより高成績でした。ゲーム未経験者に一人称視点のシューティングを1日1時間・計10時間遊んでもらう実験でも、テトリス組より注意課題の成績が伸びています。ただし小規模で、若い成人が中心の研究です。
・Bediou et al.(Psychological Bulletin, 2018): 2000〜2015年の研究をまとめたメタ分析(過去の研究を集めて統合する方法)で、プレイヤーと非プレイヤーの差は平均 g≈0.55。100人ずつ並べたとき、プレイヤーの「真ん中の人」が非プレイヤーの上から30番目あたりに入る、というざっくりした換算です。ただ、これは「もともと得意な人がゲームを選んでいる」可能性を除けない比較。訓練実験の平均は g≈0.34と小さく、比較的はっきりしていたのは「注意の向け方」と「空間認知」でした。
・Boot et al.(Acta Psychologica, 2008): 熟練ゲーマーは多くの課題で高成績でしたが、未経験者に20時間あまり遊んでもらっても、広い課題での改善は限定的でした。

つまり「ゲームで認知能力全般が上がる」とまでは言えない、というのがなかなか面白いところです。しかも対象は家庭用ゲーム機やPCの一人称視点ゲームで、ライトガン遊びも、この製品も測っていません。

話題の中心は？ Kickstarter(2025年6月24日〜8月23日)で目標700万円に対し1.5億円超、約5,900人が支援しました。ナムコ作品をアーケードで遊んだレトロ好きと、ブラウン管が消えたあとSindenやGun4IRなど液晶向けライトガンで工夫してきた愛好家の間で注目され、海外Redditの r/lightgunshooters にも、精度やテレビ設定を検証するスレッドが立っています。

注意点も。精度は環境しだいで、46インチ級OLED・2〜3m・暗めの部屋ではかなり正確という海外レビューがある一方、素早く狙いを振ると追従が遅れる、わずかに揺れる、起動ごとにキャリブレーションが必要、大きなテレビほど離れて遊ぶ必要がある、という声もあります。Amazonの評価は確認時点で5点中3.2(45件)と賛否が分かれています。ACアダプターは付属せず、USB-C(5V/3A以上)の電源が別に必要です。二人で遊ぶならアルティメット(銃2丁)。達成電器は日本法人で、親会社は中国・深圳のDashine Electronicsです。
買う前に、ソファからテレビまでの距離をメジャーで測ってみるのがよさそうです。

気になったらチェック 👇 #PR #広告
https://t.co/iH9w4q42hq

出典: Green & Bavelier, Nature, 2003 / Bediou et al., Psychological Bulletin, 2018 / Boot et al., Acta Psychologica, 2008

―――

Why did old light guns stop working on LCD TVs? 🎯

A CRT doesn't light up all at once: a glowing dot sweeps down the screen line by line, about 60 times a second. The sensor in an old light gun noted the instant that light passed by and used the timing to work out where you were aiming. (Think of a lighthouse: if you know when the beam hits you, you know where it was pointing.) An LCD keeps each pixel lit and the TV processes the picture internally, so that "timing cue" is reportedly no longer usable.

Enter G'AIM'E x Time Crisis, released in Japan on November 13, 2025. The maker says it solves the problem with sight instead of timing: a high-resolution camera plus AI to recognize the screen (no sensor bar, plugs into HDMI, officially licensed by Bandai Namco). The Premium set has four built-in games (Time Crisis, Gunbullet/Point Blank, Steel Gunner 1 and 2) and a foot pedal: press to pop out and shoot, release to duck, like the arcade cabinet.

So what do shooting games do to attention? 🤔
- Green & Bavelier (Nature, 2003): habitual action-game players scored higher than non-players on visual attention tasks. In a training experiment, non-players who played a first-person shooter for 1 hour a day, 10 hours in total, improved more on attention tasks than a Tetris group. Small samples, mostly young adults.
- Bediou et al. (Psychological Bulletin, 2018): a meta-analysis (a study that pools earlier studies) of 2000-2015 research. Players vs non-players: average g≈0.55. Roughly, line up 100 non-players and the typical player would land about 30th from the top. But this comparison can't rule out that people who are already good choose these games. Training studies averaged a smaller g≈0.34, and the clearer evidence was for top-down attention and spatial cognition.
- Boot et al. (Acta Psychologica, 2008): expert gamers did better on many tasks, yet giving non-gamers about 20 hours of practice didn't produce broad improvements.

So "games raise cognition across the board" is not established, which I find rather interesting. These studies also used console/PC first-person games, not light-gun play, and none of them tested this product.

Who's talking about it? Its Kickstarter (June 24 to August 23, 2025) raised over 150 million yen against a 7 million yen goal, from about 5,900 backers. Interest came from retro arcade fans who grew up on Namco games and from light-gun hobbyists who had been working around the loss of CRTs with LCD-friendly guns such as Sinden and Gun4IR. Reddit's r/lightgunshooters has threads checking its accuracy and TV settings.

Caveats: accuracy depends on your room. One review found it quite accurate on a 46-inch OLED at about 2-3 m in a dim room, while others report lag when you swing the aim quickly, slight jitter, recalibration at each start, and bigger screens needing more distance. Its https://t.co/J2QER6chwS rating was 3.2 out of 5 (45 ratings) when I checked. The AC adapter isn't included (USB-C, 5V/3A or more). For two players, the Ultimate set has two guns. Tassei Denki is a Japan-based company whose parent is Dashine Electronics of Shenzhen, China.
Tip: measure the distance from your sofa to the TV before you buy.

Four white men abducted a college student at gunpoint from a car outside a dance in 1959 and assaulted her.

Then something happened that had never happened in Florida: an all-white jury convicted all four of them.
Betty Jean Owens. Tallahassee.

She was a student at Florida A&M. Her three friends escaped and went straight to the police. Officers found the car and arrested the men that night — which was itself unusual.

The men confessed. And Betty Jean Owens did the thing the entire system was built to prevent: she testified, in open court, in front of them, and did not waver.

Florida A&M students shut the campus down and packed the courthouse every day of the trial.

All four were convicted and sentenced to life.
It was the first time in Florida's history that white men received life sentences for raping a Black woman.

She was 18 years old and she changed what was possible in that state by refusing to stay silent in a room full of men who assumed she would.

Betty's case was historic—but it also exposes how rarely Black women received that kind of justice for crimes committed against them.
